data.hypothesis: This distinct hybrid tests whether SIMD can capture later ASCII spans without paying for a SIMD restart after each decoded code point: skip complete 16-byte ASCII vectors, then strictly decode a 64-byte window after a mixed vector before resuming SIMD. It may help if the official mixed-width input has later ASCII spans; otherwise the scalar windows may add overhead. The fallback begins at a code-point boundary and validates the first high-bit byte rather than assuming it is a lead. No speedup is claimed.

memory_lessons.applicability: Compare hybrid variants only on the official mixed-width workload; these measurements do not establish which input feature caused the timing differences.
memory_lessons.claim: Measured valid SIMD-assisted variants span both sides of the 49.62 µs baseline: 31112ea757f04c4a measured 39.98 µs, while cd2a550c3b714843 measured 55.14 µs. The 16-byte block-boundary variant 6af9a1e290384d22 measured 49.02 µs. Correctness alone does not establish a performance benefit.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this bounded-reentry hybrid on the official mixed-width n=65536 workload and correctness cases; if it is a leading candidate, seek independent confirmation.

data.notes: One new hybrid experiment, distinct from whole-buffer validation and the one-way prefix approach. The supplied context has selected_parent=null; this proposal is based on the current src/candidate.cpp and imports no source ideas. Historical search measurements are context only; no new correctness or performance result is asserted.
transformations: Added a strict single-code-point scalar decoder and used it for scalar validation, preserving UTF-8 checks for overlong encodings, surrogates, out-of-range code points, and malformed continuations.

Skipped only complete 16-byte vectors whose bytes are all ASCII; after a mixed vector, decoded a scalar window through at least 64 bytes before resuming SIMD at the resulting known code-point boundary.
Kept vector loads within length, delegated the tail to scalar validation, and preserved the run ABI and output.
